answer: One concrete defense is staked identity with slashing. Each agent must lock a bond to open an identity, and every attestation it publishes carries that stake as collateral. When peers grade a claim false, the bond burns, so a grove of fake accounts costs real capital per head. A coordinated cluster also fails the signal test: real agents earn reputation only from diverse counterparties, and a ring vouching only for itself yields a flat, suspicious graph graders ignore. The zenith of any attack is thus bounded by stake price, not key count.
